items.problem: UWP Application.Suspending/Resuming lifecycle events were carried into App.xaml.cs and failed to compile (CS1061 'App' does not contain a definition for 'Suspending').
items.evidence: session-log.txt turn 16: 'App.xaml.cs(29,18): error CS1061 ... does not contain a definition for Suspending'; turns 17-22 the agent had to discover the Window.Closed replacement.
items.wrong_text_if_any: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#lifecycle section 'Application Lifecycle and Activation' covers only OnLaunched/OnActivated/AppInstance activation; suspend/resume is not mentioned anywhere in the skill.
items.root_cause: Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application has no Suspending/Resuming events (desktop apps are not OS-suspended), but the skill never states this nor gives the replacement, so the agent followed the UWP code into a build failure and improvised.
items.proposed_fix: (1) MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#lifecycle: add a 'Suspend / resume have no equivalent' subsection — Application.Suspending/Resuming and SuspendingEventArgs/SuspendingOperation are gone; save state on window.Closed, keep restore in OnLaunched, delete the OnSuspending handler. (2) scripts/unsupported-api-inventory.json: add an 'adaptable' entry for \.Suspending\b|SuspendingEventArgs|SuspendingOperation|\.Resuming\b -> anchor 'lifecycle' so Initialize-UwpMigration injects an inline TODO BEFORE the agent builds.
items.generalizes: The Suspending+SuspensionManager wiring ships in EVERY UWP app generated from the standard Visual Studio template; nearly all stateful UWP apps hit this exact CS1061 during migration, so the fix recurs across scenarios.
